If coadministration is unavoidable, obtain ECGs at initiation, during concomitant use, and as clinically indicated. Discontinue if the QTc interval exceeds 500 ms or if there is a change from baseline greater than 60 ms. 2. Erythromycin lactobionate and glasdegib both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor closely for increased risk of QTc prolongation. 3. Goserelin increases erythromycin lactobionate levels via QTc interval prolongation. Use caution and monitor closely. This combination increases the risk of torsades de pointes. 4. Granisetron and erythromycin lactobionate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 5. Grapefruit increases erythromycin lactobionate levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 6. Griseofulvin decreases erythromycin lactobionate levels by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 7. Erythromycin lactobionate increases guanfacine levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors significantly increase guanfacine plasma concentrations. For extended-release guanfacine, reduce the dose to half the recommended amount when coadministered. No specific recommendations are available for immediate-release guanfacine. 8. Erythromycin lactobionate and haloperidol both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 9. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the effects of heparin by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 10. Histrelin increases erythromycin lactobionate levels via QTc interval prolongation. Use caution and monitor closely. This combination increases the risk of torsades de pointes. 11. Erythromycin lactobionate increases hydrocortisone levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Hydrocortisone decreases erythromycin lactobionate levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 12. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and erythromycin lactobionate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 13. Erythromycin lactobionate increases hydroxyprogesterone caproate levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 14. Hydroxyzine increases erythromycin lactobionate toxicity via QTc interval prolongation. Use caution and monitor closely. This combination increases the risk of torsades de pointes. 15. Erythromycin lactobionate increases ibrutinib levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce the ibrutinib dose to 280 mg daily for B-cell malignancies or 420 mg daily for graft-versus-host disease when coadministered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Resume the previous dose after discontinuation of the CYP3A4 inhibitor. 16. Erythromycin lactobionate and ibutilide both prolong the QTc interval. This combination is contraindicated. 17. Idelalisib increases erythromycin lactobionate levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Idelalisib is a strong CYP3A inhibitor; avoid coadministration with sensitive CYP3A substrates. 18. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases ifosfamide levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. CYP3A4 inhibitors may reduce ifosfamide metabolism, potentially decreasing its therapeutic effects. 19. Erythromycin lactobionate and iloperidone both prolong the QTc interval. Iloperidone increases erythromycin lactobionate levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 20. Erythromycin lactobionate increases imatinib levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Imipramine and erythromycin lactobionate both prolong the QTc interval. Erythromycin lactobionate increases imipramine levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 22. Erythromycin lactobionate increases indacaterol levels by modulating P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4 activities. Use caution and monitor closely. No dose adjustment is warranted at the 75 mcg dose. 23. Erythromycin lactobionate and indapamide both prolong the QTc interval. This combination is contraindicated. 24. Erythromycin lactobionate increases indinavir levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Indinavir increases erythromycin lactobionate levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 25. Erythromycin lactobionate increases infigratinib levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 26. Inotuzumab and erythromycin lactobionate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, obtain ECGs and electrolytes before and after initiation and monitor periodically as clinically indicated. 27. Erythromycin lactobionate increases irinotecan levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 28. Erythromycin lactobionate increases isavuconazonium sulfate levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Isoflurane and erythromycin lactobionate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 30. Isoniazid increases erythromycin lactobionate levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 31. Erythromycin lactobionate increases isradipine levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Istradefylline increases erythromycin lactobionate levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Consider dose reduction of sensitive P-gp substrates. 33. Erythromycin lactobionate increases itraconazole levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Itraconazole increases erythromycin lactobionate levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 34. Erythromycin lactobionate increases ivabradine levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of ivabradine with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 35. Ivacaftor increases erythromycin lactobionate levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Erythromycin lactobionate increases ivacaftor levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce the ivacaftor dose when coadministered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 36. Erythromycin lactobionate increases ivermectin levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Erythromycin lactobionate increases ivosidenib levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of QTc-prolonging drugs with ivosidenib. 38. Erythromycin lactobionate increases ixabepilone levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 39. Ketoconazole increases erythromycin lactobionate levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Erythromycin lactobionate increases ketoconazole levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 40. Erythromycin lactobionate increases lansoprazole levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 41. Erythromycin lactobionate increases lapatinib levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 42. Erythromycin lactobionate increases larotrectinib levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Lasmiditan increases erythromycin lactobionate levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 44. Lefamulin increases erythromycin lactobionate levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Lefamulin is contraindicated with CYP3A substrates known to prolong the QT interval. 45. Erythromycin lactobionate increases lemborexant levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of lemborexant with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors. 46. Lenacapavir increases erythromycin lactobionate levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Lenacapavir, a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor, may increase the risk of adverse reactions of CYP3A4 substrates initiated within nine months after the last subcutaneous dose of lenacapavir. 47. Leniolisib increases erythromycin lactobionate levels by inhibiting OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 transporters. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 48. Erythromycin lactobionate and lenvatinib both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Lenvatinib prescribing information recommends close ECG monitoring when coadministered with QT-prolonging drugs. 49. Letermovir increases erythromycin lactobionate levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Leuprolide increases erythromycin lactobionate toxicity via QTc interval prolongation. Use caution and monitor closely. This combination increases the risk of torsades de pointes. 51. Erythromycin lactobionate increases levamlodipine levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Coadministration with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors may require dose reduction of amlodipine. Monitor for symptoms of hypotension and edema to determine the need for dose adjustment. 52. Erythromycin lactobionate and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 53. Levoketoconazole increases erythromycin lactobionate levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism.
